department: Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences, College of Sciences (Engineering & Applied Science Ph.D.)

deadline.value: Fall admission deadline is March 15, 2027 (Spring: November 15; Summer: May 1); apply by March 1, 2027 for Graduate School Awards consideration.
deadline.quote: Earth and Environmental Sciences, M.S., Ph.D. | College of Sciences Phd Degree Requirements ... Spring Admission: November 15 | Summer Admission: May 1 | Fall Admission: March 15

also.quote: Apply by March 1st to be considered

gre_general.value: A combined GRE score of at least 300 is required (alongside 3.0+ GPA).
gre_general.quote: The main requirements for entering graduate programs in EES are meeting the GRE (300 combined score), GPA criteria (3.0), and finding an EES Faculty member who will agree to be your advisor prior to being accepted into the Department.

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for Earth or Environmental Sciences; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics, and Psychology.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Applicants must contact EES faculty in advance and secure a faculty advisor's agreement to supervise them before admission; applications without an identified EES mentor will not be considered.
supervisor.quote: In addition, applicants must previously contact faculty for available positions in their research groups; faculty must be in agreement to supervise students at the time of evaluation. Students without a faculty advisor will not be considered.

funding.value: Departmental funding is competitive in the form of teaching assistantships (TA) and faculty grant-funded research assistantships (RA), alongside university tuition and out-of-state fee scholarships.
funding.quote: Funding within the department is also available. This type of funding is competitive and is in the form of teaching assistantships (TA), or research assistantships (RA). RAs are typically funded through extramural funding sources secured by individual faculty in their field of expertise.

entry_route.value: Preference is given to applicants holding a Master's degree in a related field (up to 30 credits transferable toward the 81-credit Ph.D.), while applicants with a strong Bachelor's transcript are also considered and complete M.S.-level coursework within the 51 coursework credits.
entry_route.quote: Possess a Bachelor’s degree (or 4-year equivalency) in a field related to one of the nine participating programs. | Preference will be given to students who possess a Master’s degree in the related field, but students whose Bachelor’s transcript demonstrate a strong academic performance will be considered.

also.quote: 81 graduate credit hours are required in total for the Ph. D. program in Engineering & Applied Science, of which 30 hours in dissertation research are required and aa minimum of 51 semester credit hours of graduate course work in an approved program beyond the Bachelor's degree. Up to 30 graduate credit hours from a Master's degree program, if the area of the Master's degree is relevant to the concentration, may be applied towards the satisfaction of credit hours for the Ph.D..

notes: Earth and Environmental Sciences concentration within the Engineering & Applied Science Ph.D.; covers both Earth Sciences and Environmental/Coastal Sciences. Ph.D. PDF notes legacy TOEFL 550 PBT (superseded by Graduate School 4.0 new scale / 79 iBT). Requires 3 references, statement of purpose, CV/resume, GRE, and EES mentor.
name: Engineering and Applied Science (Earth & Environmental Sciences)
